title: Control Trace Collector for Data Lifecycle & Retention Audits
creator: Priya Mehta
description: Goal: build a repeatable, auditable collector and orchestration layer that maps compliance controls for data lifecycle (ingest, store, access, movement, deletion) into verifiable artifacts for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits. The feature will centralize control-to-source mappings, collect normalized evidence from runtime components (storage, DB, KMS, runtime audit logs), produce time-boxed 'proofpacks' with signed manifests and integrity hashes, and expose UI/API endpoints for auditors and customer compliance teams. Must respect data residency and retention policies per region and ensure no PII is included in exported artifacts (use deterministic hashing/redaction).
approach: Phased delivery: (1) mapping engine + metadata model for control->source->evidence type, (2) lightweight collectors for S3/Blob storage metadata, RDS/Postgres audit tables, Redwood runtime request traces and KV cache lifecycle events, (3) retention snapshotter that records policy state and deletion events, (4) proofpack generator that bundles artifacts, computes SHA256 manifests, signs with HSM-backed key, and writes to a WORM-backed bucket, (5) compliance console views and API endpoints for scheduled or ad-hoc exports. Operate under per-customer isolation; collectors emit only hashed identifiers and metadata by default. Integrate with Dedicated/Private deployments via the private control plane agent.
acceptance_criteria: Mapping engine can encode SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls and map each control to one or more evidence source patterns (events, configs, snapshots)
Collectors produce normalized evidence items with schema (timestamp, source, region, artifact_type, artifact_reference, integrity_hash) and do not include raw PII fields
Retention snapshotter records policy state and last-deletion cursors by region for a given customer and can export snapshots for an arbitrary date range

Proofpack generator emits a signed manifest (SHA256) and package stored in a WORM bucket with a verifiable signature; proofpack includes human-readable index and minimal redacted extracts for auditors
Console shows per-customer compliance readiness score with missing-evidence warnings and drill-down links to artifacts
API supports scheduled weekly exports and on-demand export with RBAC and audit logging
Collectors and proofpack generation validated with end-to-end test harness and pass security review
Collectors scale to target workload: 1M normalized events/day across 1000 customers without >99th percentile latency impact on serving runtime
comments: 2026-03-02 Marco Nguyen: Kickoff—aligned on mapping engine schema. Decided to normalize to a small set of artifact types to simplify proofs (config_snapshot, access_log, deletion_record, key_rotation).

2026-03-04 Elena Garcia (Security): Recommended HSM signing for manifests and explicit redaction rules to prevent accidental export of PII. Raised requirement for a threat model and optional ephemeral artifacts for forensic review.

2026-03-06 Priya Mehta: PM note—prioritize S3/RDS collectors in phase 1 because they cover the majority of customer evidence. Deprioritizing application-level full-request dumps for now due to privacy risk.

2026-03-08 Marco Nguyen: Engineering tradeoff discussion—store raw logs encrypted for 90 days vs only storing hashed indices and on-demand retrieval. Opted for hashed indices + short-lived encrypted vault for retrieval with strict access controls.

risks: Accidental inclusion of PII in proofpacks if collectors are misconfigured—mitigation: redaction rules and schema validation
Cross-region evidence linking complexity when customers span multiple cloud regions—mitigation: canonical region mapping and per-region manifests
HSM availability impacting scheduled proofpack signing—mitigation: failover to audit-only unsigned packages with elevated alerting
